subject: Re: Data use commitments for BrightBridge pilot — ownership, no-training, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbridgehealth.com, legal@brightbridgehealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data use commitments for BrightBridge pilot — ownership, no-training, and subprocessors

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and routing features look promising for the pilot. Legal and procurement asked me to follow up with a clear statement of commitments we need to finalize the SOW and DPA redlines. High-level asks from our side:

- A written commitment that BrightBridge customer data (including prompts and model responses) will not be used to train or improve any Redwood-hosted models (no-training / no-model-improvement).
- Clarification on output/response IP: we need BrightBridge to retain ownership of generated responses for our customers (for downstream licensing and audit).
- A current subprocessor inventory and confirmation of any planned subprocessor changes during the pilot.
- Evidence of operational controls: onshore KMS usage options, ephemeral KV caching, and whether telemetry or aggregated logs will contain PII or prompt content.

I've attached our draft redlines to the DPA (BrightBridge-DPA-redlines.pdf) — procurement is hoping we can get a clean signal this week so they can move to PO. If you can share the subprocessor list and SOC2 summary, that helps accelerate internal review.

Do you have a succinct statement you can share about the no-training commitment and what operational evidence we can provide?

Appreciate it —
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Head of Procurement, BrightBridge Health

--- Attachment stubs: BrightBridge-DPA-redlines.pdf (annotated DPA, 7 pages)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for BrightBridge pilot — ownership, no-training, and subprocessors

Hi Sasha,

Thanks — glad the demo was useful. Short answer up front: we can commit to a contractual prohibition on using BrightBridge customer prompts and responses to train, fine-tune, or improve our hosted models for the duration of the pilot and any active contract term, subject to a small set of operational clarifications below. I summarize the scope and what we can deliver as evidence.

Commitment (draft language we usually propose):
- "Redwood Inference shall not use, incorporate, or otherwise employ Customer-provided prompts, responses, or other Customer Content for training, fine-tuning, or improving Redwood models or model weights. Customer Content will be processed only to provide the contracted inference service and related operational troubleshooting."

Operational clarifications and proven evidence we can provide:
1) Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_2026-01.csv). Any changes during the pilot will be notified 30 days in advance; for emergency replacements we provide immediate notice and a remediation plan.
2) KMS/residency: we support onshore KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted pilots we offer onshore key wrapping and will provide a configuration checklist.
3) Ephemeral KV / caching: runtime KV is ephemeral per-session; we can provide an architecture diagram and a sanitized trace showing prefix caching disabled for the pilot if desired.
4) Telemetry and logs: aggregated telemetry (metrics, error traces) does not include prompt text by default. Audit logs containing request/response payloads are stored in redactable form and can be exported to an onshore SFTP or API for customer custody per the DPA.
5) SOC2 Summary: attached SOC2_summary_2025.pdf and we can share more detailed artifacts under an NDA.

Next steps I propose:
- Legal redline session: Jordan can join to walk through procurement redlines and technical implications.
- Provide a short "evidence pack" (sanitized architecture diagram, a redacted audit export, and the subprocessor CSV) for your security team to verify.

I'll attach the files and loop in David for privacy nuances. Happy to revise the draft language to match BrightBridge's form of words.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment stubs: subprocessors_2026-01.csv (current subprocessor registry)

From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@brightbridgehealth.com, procurement@brightbridgehealth.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for BrightBridge pilot — ownership, no-training, and subprocessors

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of follow-ups from legal after a quick pass:

- The DPA redlines request a perpetual prohibition on using BrightBridge data for model improvement (our preference). If you can only commit for the contract term, please state that explicitly and we'll mark our redlines accordingly.
- On output IP: we need clearer language that allows BrightBridge to license generated responses to our downstream customers without restriction.
- For telemetry: legal is concerned about aggregated signals that could be re-identified. Can you state whether any telemetry (sampling, usage patterns) could include prompt-derived tokens in any pipeline (debugging snapshots, QA captures)? If there's any case where full payloads are captured, we need an assurance on retention and access controls.

Procurement also asked whether you can provide a redlined DPA response inline (PDF) so they can quickly accept/reject line items. We'll also need a SOC2 bridge letter or a pointer to where we can validate the most recent attestation.

If you can provide the short evidence pack you mentioned and a proposed response to the three bullets above, we should be able to circulate internally by EOD and push PO.

Best,
Sasha

--- Attachment referenced: BrightBridge-DPA-redlines.pdf (their annotated copy)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@brightbridgehealth.com>, legal@brightbridgehealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for BrightBridge pilot — ownership, no-training, and subprocessors

Hi Sasha and BrightBridge team —

Thanks for the clear list. To address legal's bullets directly:

1) Term of commitment: we can accept a contractual prohibition limited to the active contract term plus a 90-day operational wind-down where retained troubleshooting artifacts may be used only to the extent necessary for debugging the pilot; we cannot make a perpetual prohibition across all customers (we can, however, make a perpetual prohibition for customer-specific data if that's BrightBridge's explicit request and we agree to escrow/operational controls — we should discuss tradeoffs).

2) Output IP: Redwood is comfortable with language that explicitly grants BrightBridge ownership and the right to sublicense generated responses produced from BrightBridge prompts during the contract term. We'll propose concise clause language for your team to insert into the DPA/SOW.

3) Telemetry: normal aggregated telemetry (metrics, counters, sampled latency histograms) never contains prompt or response tokens. For debugging we may capture snapshots that include payloads; those are gated behind role-based access, are time-limited (default retention 30 days), and we can provide onshore export or redaction on request. We will commit to:
   - Providing a sanitized sample export for your security review,
   - Disabling automatic payload snapshotting for the pilot unless BrightBridge requests and approves it, and
   - Exporting any captured payload snapshots to your SFTP or API on request and deleting our retained copy within 7 days of export.

Attachments included: SOC2_summary_2025.pdf (summary; full report available under NDA) and a redlined DPA response template we can return inline if you send the PDF back. Jordan, can you prepare the technical evidence pack (arch diagram + redacted audit sample) and a suggested DPA clause set for output IP?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize language.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment stubs: SOC2_summary_2025.pdf
